clue.text: Where the icing on the cake may be too much

definitions.text: Where the icing on the cake may be too much

parts.words: Where the icing on the cake may be too much
parts.note: icing sits at the very summit of a cake, and the same phrase means excessive or exaggerated

explanation.surface: A baker's worry that the decoration is excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is placed on the upper surface of a cake, and the idiom also means excessive, so both readings meet.

clue.text: Pained expression in appreciation of a hit out of bounds

indicators.note: the word loses its boundaries, the first and last letters

parts.note: touché is what a fencer says to acknowledge a hit

explanation.surface: A cry of pain from someone struck by a wild shot.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUCHE, the fencer's acknowledgement, loses its outer T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is the exclamation one gives when hurt, a pained cry.

clue.text: Reserved English artist returning on old boat in sea

indicators.note: in a down clue the artist abbreviation comes back up the column

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: the boat sits inside the sea word

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
Noah's Ark is the ancient vessel

explanation.surface: An English painter coming home aboard an old boat at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked means set aside or reserved for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Tigerish wingers Everton's opening half-time topic

indicators.note: the wingers are the outermost letters, like players on the flanks
the opening letter of the football club's name
the second half of the word time is used

explanation.surface: A football team talk at the interval about Everton's fierce wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club; 'half-time' gives ME, the latter half of TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Benefit from past conspiracy having taken one in

parts.note: ex means former or past, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: the conspiracy word takes something into itself
completes the container signal, putting the numeral inside

parts.note: a plot is a secret conspiracy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Profiting from an old scheme that took someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it for gain, to profit from it.

clue.text: End with warning about bank payment on time

indicators.note: the warning word goes about, around, the payment

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign
DD is a direct debit, a bank payment

explanation.surface: A final letter from the bank threatening action on an overdue payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover piece, an odd end or remnant.

clue.text: Cast-iron case for prison

indicators.note: the hyphenated words act as a case holding the letters of the answer within them

explanation.surface: A cast-iron housing designed to hold a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is long-standing British slang for a jail, as in 'doing time in stir'.

clue.text: Make adjustments to width cutting timber

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the timber word, going inside it

parts.note: teak is a hard timber

explanation.surface: Adjusting the width when sawing wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak is to make small adjustments or fine-tune something.

clue.text: Edit what comes in?

parts.note: in a down entry, the word TIDE rising up the column reads as the clue's own word

explanation.surface: An editor asking what material has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Read upwards, as rising in a down light, TIDE gives the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising tide is the sea coming in, the flood tide.

clue.text: Loathes type found in Norfolk town

indicators.note: the type word is placed inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, a county in eastern England
the like of something is its type or kind

explanation.surface: A person who hates a certain kind of person found in a small English town.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislike something is to have an aversion to it; loathing is a stronger form.

clue.text: Caught Gaelic as spoken word — crude language

indicators.note: the letters built from the first two pieces are to be pronounced, and the result heard as a word

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught; Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: Someone overheard using rude Gaelic words.
explanation.walkthrough: C plus ERSE is said 'kurse', which sounds the same as the swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word or oath is crude language, the usual everyday sense of a curse.

clue.text: End gossip about obesity

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are turned about, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: Stop spreading rumours about someone's weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but here it rearranges ENDGOSSIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Podginess is plumpness or fatness, a milder synonym for being overweight.

clue.text: Pay attention — entry gate ahead!

indicators.note: the piece for 'gate' goes in front of the piece for 'entry'

parts.note: the gate is the money taken at a match, also called the take
a note is a brief entry jotted in a diary or record

explanation.surface: A warning sign: watch out, there is an entrance gate coming up.
explanation.definitionFit: To take note is an idiom meaning to notice carefully or heed something.

clue.text: Point out the similarity of so-called moss

indicators.note: the word is as it is called aloud, i.e. as it sounds

parts.note: lichen is loosely a moss-like growth on rocks and trees

explanation.surface: Asking whether a plant truly deserves its name of moss.
explanation.walkthrough: Lichen is not strictly a moss, which is why 'so-called' sits comfortably in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them, showing how they resemble each other.

clue.text: The samurai could be surprisingly incompetent

indicators.note: the letters could form a surprising arrangement, i.e. a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A Japanese warrior who turns out to be unexpectedly unskilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish means unprofessional and inept, lacking skill.

clue.text: Fill in claim

definitions.meaning: to complete a form or cheque, as in writing one out
to allege or pretend, as in 'he tried to ... he was ill'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both writing out a document and asserting something that may not be true.

clue.text: Love greenery after change of heart in The Hebrides maybe

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: the central letter of the greenery word is changed, and this follows the love piece

parts.note: verdure is lush green vegetation

explanation.surface: Loving the green landscape of the Scottish islands after a change of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides Overture is a concert piece by Mendelssohn; VERDURE's middle D becomes T.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's The Hebrides is an example of an orchestral opening piece of this kind.

clue.text: Dispatch date

definitions.meaning: to escort someone on an outing, as in taking a partner out for dinner

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to kill someone and to go out with them socially.

clue.text: In the past small price increases initially left fifty people moving from crowded city

parts.note: something over is finished and in the past
P is a penny, a price

indicators.note: only the first letter of increases is used

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Rising prices once drove fifty people out of a crowded city.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspill is the surplus population rehoused from a congested city into new towns.

clue.text: Most orderly trial involving African dictator

indicators.note: the trial word wraps round the dictator's name

parts.note: a test is a trial or examination
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda in the 1970s

explanation.surface: An efficiently run court case against a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiest is the superlative of tidy, meaning neatest or most well arranged.

clue.text: Nothing outwardly classic in farewell piece of music

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the farewell word

parts.note: ta-ta is a casual British goodbye
O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: only the outside letters of classic are used

explanation.surface: A classic farewell piece of music with nothing special about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard composition, a kind of musical piece.

clue.text: Fashionable tweeds dominating northern shopping centre

indicators.note: read as 'fashioned into a new shape', so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Smart tweed clothing is all the rage in a shopping centre up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dominating' is a link here; TWEEDS and N are reworked together as one pool.
explanation.definitionFit: London's West End is a major area for shops and theatres, a famous retail district.

clue.text: Wind resulting from change in weather

indicators.note: the answer is the weather word with its letters changed round

explanation.surface: Wind blowing as the weather turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like a noun for moving air, but is the verb to twist round.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreathe is to wind or twist around something, as smoke wreathes a chimney.

clue.text: Eager crowd in distress

parts.note: up for something means keen or eager
a set is a group or crowd of people

explanation.surface: An excited mob in a state of distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upset means being troubled or distressed, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Splendid meal lacking source of protein

indicators.note: the meal word is without a letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

indicators.note: the source of protein is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A great meal even without much protein.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal for excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Confused cavers heading for chasm

indicators.note: the letters of the cavers word are muddled up

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass heading

explanation.surface: Lost potholers make their way towards a deep gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like 'going towards', but heading is a compass direction, SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack in a glacier, a kind of gaping chasm.

clue.text: Cold potato in Indian cookery's fine

parts.note: aloo is the Hindi word for potato, as in aloo gobi
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Cold potato in a curry is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and unfriendly, figuratively cold.

clue.text: Almost lavish bonus

indicators.note: almost all of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: plush means luxurious or lavish

explanation.surface: An extravagant extra payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or extra benefit.

clue.text: Bronze aboard ship in main

indicators.note: the colour word goes on board, inside, the ship-in word

parts.note: to import goods is to ship them in from abroad
a tan is a bronzed skin colour

explanation.surface: A bronze statue carried on a vessel out on the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like the sea, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Main as an adjective means chief or principal, a synonym for something of great significance.

clue.text: One can see through this coercive (now and then) Labour leader

indicators.note: taking letters only some of the time, i.e. every other one
the opening letter heads the word Labour

explanation.surface: A Labour party chief who is sometimes heavy-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a projecting bay window, something one looks out through.

clue.text: Reporter's about to be replaced by raw beginner, 12

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out and another put in its place

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, a reporter
C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the beginning letter of the word raw

explanation.surface: A journalist about to be supplanted by a green novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 refers to the answer at 12-across, which means listen or pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Hark is an old command meaning listen, the same as paying attention.

clue.text: 'Victoria' perhaps a composition of Fats Waller?

indicators.note: the letters are composed, put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether 'Victoria' is a song written by the jazz pianist Fats Waller.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria Falls in Africa is an example; the surface pretends Victoria is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Falls is one of the world's great cascades, an example of the plural.
